title: test(scripts): batch 10c pilot (Tier C) — per-entry recipe-A partitions for check-durability-degradation-log-level
body:
Part of #13799 — BATCH 10c, the **Tier C PILOT** for the per-entry partition shape
(census design question 2, option C), on ONE file:
`scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs` (~6.4 kloc, wired as
`check:durability-log-level`).

## Why this file needed a shape of its own

It is TWO recipe-A self-tests sharing a module. `selfTest()` and
`selfTestReadSeams()` each own a literal `cases` table, its own driving loop and
its own verdict; one `--self-test` dispatch runs both. `failures === 0` was each
entry's only success condition, so "every case held" and "the cases never ran"
printed the same line — twice, independently.

The card's row-3 description was re-verified against the file before any edit and
holds in every particular: flag handshake, two entry functions, two literal
tables with a `name:` label field, a verdict per entry, derived counts 63 + 57
(confirmed on a run, not read off the source), 16 banner comments inside the two
tables.

## What landed

1. **ONE module-level `SELF_TEST_BATTERIES`, partitioned per entry** — an object
   per entry (`selfTest`, `selfTestReadSeams`), each keyed by that entry's own row
   labels verbatim, floor 1 per row. Chosen over one flat map plus a literal
   partition list for two measured reasons stated at the site: the flat shape
   needs all 120 labels written twice (two literals that drift apart silently),
   and it COLLAPSES a label present in both tables into one key — which this file
   actually had, so the flat roster would have held 119 batteries for 120 rows
   with the second row's floor met by the first row running.
2. **A size pin PER PARTITION** in one frozen map (`selfTest: 63`,
   `selfTestReadSeams: 57`) plus **the roster total** (`120`). One frozen map
   rather than two bare constants so a new partition cannot be added with no pin
   at all. The total is checked from BOTH verdict sites: each entry reads only its
   own partition, so a partition deleted whole is invisible to every per-partition
   pin — the deleted partition is exactly the one nobody checks.
3. **`registerCase(name)` first in each driving loop**, before anything a case can
   skip past. No `battery()` opener: for a table-driven self-test the ROW is the
   battery, so attribution is the loop variable.
4. **The floor at each entry's OWN verdict site**, before its success line, over
   its own partition only. Every refusal names the partition and the row.
5. **Cross-checked both ways per partition** (every declared row registered;
   every registration declared), with duplicate refusal **within** a partition and
   **across** partitions — the latter in two forms: a label declared in two
   rosters, and a row registering under a label declared in a *different*
   partition.
6. **The 16 `// ──` banners inside the two tables are NOT batteries** — the rows
   are. Said at the roster and again at each verdict site; no banner is promoted,
   all stay comments. Flooring 16 sections instead of 120 cases would leave a
   section "run" while every row under it stopped.

**The one cross-table collision, and what was done about it.** Measured, not
assumed: the two tables shared exactly one label —
`flags: the inner catch itself is still judged (no coverage lost to shadowing)` —
describing an analogous nesting fixture in each rule. It is **namespaced**, not
refused: the read-seam table's row now reads `... is still judged for a READ seam
...`, matching that table's own voice (its neighbouring row already says
"consumed the read" where the log-level table says "consumed the call"), with a
comment at the site saying why. This is the only case-facing text this PR changes,
and it is the only line of `--self-test` output that differs from the installed
base.

## Scope discipline

No assertion condition, message or argument is changed. The whole diff deletes
**three** lines: the two red verdict lines, reworded to recipe A's
`N failure(s) (cases and floor)`, and the namespaced label. Both green lines are
byte-identical to the installed base. The flag handshake
(`selfTestReachedVerdict` / `readSeamsReachedVerdict`) is untouched and stays
orthogonal to the floor — see ablation (f).

## Evidence

**Production mode is byte-identical.** Against the installed base worktree at the
same pin, all three non-self-test modes, stdout AND stderr, `cmp`:

```
CMP prod.out IDENTICAL     CMP prod.err IDENTICAL
CMP list.out IDENTICAL     CMP list.err IDENTICAL
CMP depth.out IDENTICAL    CMP depth.err IDENTICAL
```

`--self-test` output diffs by exactly one line (the namespaced label), and both
verdicts are unchanged: `✓ self-test (log-level rule): 63 case(s) passed` /
`✓ self-test (read-seam invention rule): 57 case(s) passed, and the baseline offer
stays marked maintainer-only (#8435)`.

**Floors measured on a run, never transcribed.** Pinning 9999 and reading the
breach line:

```
✗ self-test floor (selfTest): SELF_TEST_BATTERIES.selfTest declares 63 batteries, below the pinned 9999 …
✗ self-test floor (selfTestReadSeams): SELF_TEST_BATTERIES.selfTestReadSeams declares 57 batteries, below the pinned 9999 …
✗ self-test floor (selfTest): the roster declares 120 batteries across all partitions, below the pinned 9999 …
```

**Ablations.** Every leg: mutation applied by an anchored mutator that REFUSES on
a zero-count anchor, proven on disk by the git blob hash moving plus a read-back
count of the injected/removed text; restored with `git checkout HEAD -- ABSPATH` and
proven by blob hash equality with the HEAD blob AND an empty `git diff HEAD`; an
`EXIT INT TERM` trap holding an absolute path. No build step is involved — this
gate is executed directly by path, resolving nothing through a package `exports`,
so there is no `dist/` for a stale artefact to hide in.

| leg | mutation | observed |
|:--|:--|:--|
| a | a row deleted from table 1 | `self-test battery "flags: catch around syncSchema logging warn" DID NOT RUN in partition "selfTest" — 0 cases registered, 1 pinned.` Zero refusals name the other partition. |
| a2 | the same, plus the pre-existing dispatch abort no-op'd | partition 2's verdict **untouched**: `✓ self-test (read-seam invention rule): 57 case(s) passed …` in the same run |
| b | a row deleted from table 2 | `… "flags: #4825 pre-fix — catch around a read returns an invented \`1\`" DID NOT RUN in partition "selfTestReadSeams"` while partition 1 prints `✓ self-test (log-level rule): 63 case(s) passed` |
| c | `registerCase()` removed from loop 1 | all 63 rows of partition 1 read DID NOT RUN (64 floor lines), all 63 cases still print `✓`, zero refusals name partition 2 |
| d | partition-1 size pin set to 999 | `SELF_TEST_BATTERIES.selfTest declares 63 batteries, below the pinned 999 …` |
| e1 | the namespacing reverted in the table only | `… registered 1 case(s) in partition "selfTestReadSeams" but is not declared there — it IS declared in partition "selfTest", so this row is either duplicated across the two tables or attributed to the wrong entry.` |
| e2 | reverted in the table AND the roster | `"flags: the inner catch itself is still judged (no coverage lost to shadowing)" is declared in BOTH partition "selfTest" and partition "selfTestReadSeams".` |
| f | an early `return` after the first case of `selfTest()` | the FLOOR prints nothing at all (its verdict site is never reached) and the HANDSHAKE catches it: `selfTest() returned without reaching its verdict`. This is the orthogonality evidence — the handshake catches a `return` that skips the verdict, the floor catches a run that REACHES the verdict having stopped running cases. |

**Instrument, before → after** (`node scripts/measure-self-test-floor.mjs --json`,
run in both worktrees): 170 rows both times; ROSTER 156 → 157, NONE 13 → 12,
COUNT 1 → 1. Exactly one row moved — this file, `NONE → ROSTER` — and **nothing
entered NONE**. `extractWatchHints` on this file is byte-identical before and
after (4 hints).

**Gates.** The derived family from
`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`
(no hand-built path list — the script took the change set from git itself), every
command, exit codes captured by redirect before any pipe.

All 23 commands ran on the final head `26a395218`. **22 exit 0.** The 23rd,
`pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates`, was RED on the first attempt for a reason this PR
caused and then fixed:

```
✗ every compound self-test NAME the anchor matches is classified in COMPOUND_ANCHOR_LEDGER
  — unlisted: scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs::checkSelfTestFloor
✗ dispatch-gates self-test: 1 of 1381 case(s) failed.
```

The shared floor helper is a compound self-test name, so the anchor fires on it.
Fixed the way that ledger's own maintenance note requires — **classified, not
renamed** ("⛔ Do not 'repair' a red by renaming the function to dodge the anchor:
the row is the record") — with one row, `accidental: false`, because it is
self-test-only machinery reached from the two verdict sites, not production code
the anchor caught by accident. Re-run on the final head, in the foreground under
the shared verify lock:

```
✓ dispatch-gates self-test: 1381 cases pass.
os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0 · held the lock 380s (6m20s) · waited 0s
```

The always-runs tail, each exit code captured by redirect before any pipe:

- `check-self-test-workflow-commands.mjs` and `--self-test` — 0 / 0
  (`… 6 declared batteries, 23 cases registered, every battery at or above its
  pinned floor.`)
- `check:declared-population-live` — 0
  (`✓ … 201 of 252 famil(ies) declare a path population, and every one of them
  reaches this tree's 7440 tracked file(s).`)
- `check-self-test-wired.mjs` and `--self-test` — 0 / 0
- `check:ratchet-remedy-authority` — 0 · `check:nul-bytes` — 0 ·
  `check:watch-hint-literal` — 0
- the file's own suite `check:durability-log-level` (which runs `--self-test`
  then the gate) — 0
- whole-repo `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`) — **0**

The derivation also flagged 7 artifact-roster families whose roster sits under a
directory this PR touches, where "silence is not evidence in EITHER direction".
All 7 were run rather than assumed: `check-published-list-mirrors` (+`--self-test`),
`check:console-injection`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:i18n-stale-fill`,
`check:pm-label-desc-cap` all exit 0. `check:published-readme-exports` exits 1 and
is **NOT MEASURED, not red**: it needs a built tree (`… dist/index.d.ts does not
exist. Build first`), and the control run of the same command in the unmodified
base worktree fails identically with the same finding count. Its `--self-test`
half is green here.

Beyond the derived family, this PR edits a gate/tool script, so that script's own
suite is owed separately: `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`'s suite IS
`check:pm-dispatch-gates` (1381 cases), quoted green above. The five test files
that grep for `dispatch-gates.mjs` were read: all five mentions are prose in
comments citing its self-test as the authority — none imports it.

Not owed and not run: CI runs the whole farm regardless. No changeset — nothing
here publishes from any package, so `skip-changeset` is on the PR.
